title: Session handoff 2026-11-19: sonnet renewal to build LCLI-797 (launcher class, DEC-282 item 7); main held, 0.15.0 cut held
description:
Session-handoff record for the lore-cli worker, 2026-11-19, written at the leader's renewal boundary. The predecessor is being renewed onto a sonnet tier SPECIFICALLY to build LCLI-797: the dispatch floor reads sonnet against deepseek-flash for that task's path (bin/lore.cjs). Restore with opum-workflow:opum-handoff; the live tracker and the live repository outrank this record. Close it once a successor has restored from it.

STATE, every ref read at 2026-11-19T04:33Z by the session that wrote this, not remembered:
- origin/dev == 983cb74f4db16466c8089a4510a9b90295eddc16 (#731, the LCLI-797 ruling note). Local dev is on that commit, working tree CLEAN, no unpushed commits, no open pull requests into dev.
- origin/main == 7b6176842e18c929039b155706b6a537130993eb, EIGHTEEN commits behind dev. It is HELD: the leader said on 2026-11-19 do not promote while the release is held. main is an ancestor of dev, so a promotion would be a plain fast-forward when it is eventually unheld.
- npm dist-tags, both @opum-ai/lore and @opum-ai/quest: latest 0.14.1, release-candidate 0.15.0-rc.1. The 0.15.0 cut is the operator's and is HELD (LCLI-775, In Progress, hold-labelled).
- 51 worktrees registered under .claude/worktrees/. None was removed, deregistered or pruned by the predecessor. DEC-208 and LCLI-740 (open) require that this stay true.

WHAT THIS SESSION LANDED (all merged, all on dev): #725 the LCLI-718 DEC-281 (a3) build at reviewed head ea0fd244, squash d0601bfc, opus round-3 verdict APPROVE, run 44424067971; #728 closed the consumed LCLI-795 handoff; #729 completed LCLI-718 and filed LCLI-796; #730 filed LCLI-797; #731 recorded the leader's option A ruling on LCLI-797. No promotion was taken, correctly.

LCLI-797 IS THE POINT OF THIS RENEWAL. State: To Do, labels [hold, launcher], bug, high. Its record carries, and a builder should read it rather than this summary: the VERBATIM DEC-282 item 7 and (a1) text, read by ref from opum-doc dev 69af243c (.quest/planning.json, decisions[DEC-282].outcome); the measurement; the fix shape; and the ruling.
- The defect, MEASURED: bin/lore.cjs leaves the native child running when the wrapper is killed. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP each killed the wrapper and the child was still alive 1.5 s later, in all three cases, with a positive control proving the liveness detector could report death. Cause: the POSIX path is one spawnSync with stdio inherit, blocking the event loop, and the file registers no signal handler.
- RULING A, leader, 2026-11-19: bin/lore.cjs IS the DEC-182 (1) launcher class, because it is the bin entry that decides which binary runs, and the rule is when unsure, sensitive. It is built by a sonnet-or-higher lore-cli worker with an opus security review and NO DeepSeek at any step. The hold stays as filed until the build lands.
- The fence, from the dispatch: stop and report if the fix needs any other DEC-182 (1) path class or adds a dependency.
- When the fix is at a green head, cut .claude/worktrees/review-<pr>-<sha7> for its review round and report. Never remove a worktree.

QUEUE, in order, for the successor:
1. LCLI-797, the launcher-class build above.
2. LCLI-791, LCLI-792, LCLI-793 (all high; DEC-282 items 1, 2 and 3): one quest task list per check/sync run cached by the .quest tree hash; an advisory lock per git common dir with result reuse and stale-holder recovery; managed-block-only drift as a warning by default and an error only under --strict. Item 4 was LCLI-718, now Done. DEC-282 says items 1 to 4 ship together in the next lore/quest pair, so these three travel with LCLI-797 in that release.
3. LCLI-794 (low, DEC-282 item 6): PROFILE lore rename at about 2000 tasks and report before changing anything. Measurement only.
4. LCLI-790 (medium, mod+hooks): the Lore pane gate opens whenever a process is interactive and CLAUDECODE is unset. LCLI-795 recorded it as waiting for a plan approval and not built because it is a hook path; re-read its record before acting rather than trusting that summary.
5. LCLI-796 (low, review-follow-up): three non-blocking minors from the #725 round-3 review. F1 the inspector-mode loops at test/ladybug-lifecycle.test.ts:298, 322, 345, 374 sit inside one test(), so a mutation shows only the first red row; F2 line 311 asserts reuse but not sourceLoads; F4 docs/reference/cli-surface.md:717-718 says an (a3) generation needs no clearing while :725 calls cache clear the first step of worktree removal, and it names a ruling where a release is meant. F3 was closed by the LCLI-718 finalization note.

HOLDS AND RULINGS A SUCCESSOR MUST KEEP:
- Do NOT promote dev to main. Main is HELD for the release (leader, 2026-11-19). When it is unheld the shape is unchanged: open a PR from dev, let the required checks go green on that exact SHA, then git push origin origin/dev:main, never the merge button.
- Do not publish, and never move a dist-tag. The 0.15.0 pair cut is the operator's first-party step, and LCLI-775 carries the hold.
- Never remove, deregister or prune any worktree, including every review-* one (DEC-208, LCLI-740 open). ADD a new review-<pr>-<sha7> per review round.
- DEC-182 (1) option A on the launcher class (above) is settled and is not to be re-litigated.
- Hold labels, each removable only when its own condition ends: LCLI-646, LCLI-760, LCLI-775, LCLI-776, LCLI-781, LCLI-782, LCLI-786, LCLI-797.
- LCLI-658 needs a sonnet-tier route before its hold label and trigger note can be written; a tracker-only edit to it was refused at the floor once already.
- DEC-282 item 7 is the most urgent of its items, because an orphaned native process is a resource leak for any caller with a timeout.

FACTS THAT COST TIME, worth not relearning:
- The local pair lock is real: the source declares lore 0.15.0 while the installed quest is 0.14.1, so bun run lore check exits 6 locally after reading the bundle clean, and the three LCLI-614 real-quest race tests fail locally. CI supplies quest 0.15.0 and is the judge.
- A tracker-only diff can still go red on infrastructure. #731's first run failed only on explorer browser qualification, because the action Install browser system deps timed out after 20 minutes; gh run rerun --failed cleared it, and #730 was the reachability control. Read WHICH job failed, not the run conclusion.
- gh pr merge --delete-branch with -R does NOT remove the LOCAL branch; check git branch --list and delete with -D (the safe -d re-checks ancestry a squash merge already broke).
- After a squash, git diff <reviewed-head> <squash> proves the landed bytes are the reviewed bytes when every path it lists is under .quest/. That is cheaper and more honest than re-running a suite that is red locally for known reasons.
- Quest refuses To Do to Done; run quest task start before task complete. A completion MOVES tasks/X.json to completed/, so stage with git add -A .quest and read --cached --stat.
- Quest writes need --actor lore-cli --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse. Pass long note text through a variable read from a file, because backticks inside double quotes are executed by the shell.

SKILLS the next session should reach for: opum-workflow:opum-handoff (restore), opum-workflow:opum-sdlc (branch, PR, promotion), opum-workflow:opum-tool-output.
